past_recommendations.text: Execute the Large-cap reversal GO suspension — now recommended at #17, #18, #19, #20 and #21 and still unshipped; Large runs cw 35.8% over 17 clusters against Medium's 64.9% over 19, five cycles running.

Ship the earliness instrumentation fix — emit `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the actual per-bucket gate; unshipped since #18, and earliness analysis is now reversal-only for a fourth consecutive cycle.

Emit cluster-weighted `entry_r` by score tier in the pre-aggregated tables (requested at #20, still row-pooled); entry_r is heavily right-skewed, so the by-score medians now driving the entry-bar verdict cannot be audited for cluster concentration.

Open a watch on moving the bounce entry bar from score 4 to score 5 — median entry_r is flat 1.54–1.80R across scores 0–4 and jumps to 2.50R only at 5; settle it when score 6 reaches 20 clusters (currently 4) so the top of the curve can be read as a trend rather than one spiking tier.

Update the priority_report CLUSTER DAY comment — the 7–14 band it cites as −0.50R/10 sessions now reads +0.10R/12 sessions, a sign flip and the third different value in three cycles; mark it single-session-sensitive and unusable as justification.
Add the thin-day damp on the 0–2 breadth band (25 sessions, EV −0.33R, win 34.5%) — the only breadth band with ≥20 sessions, and the EV gradient across bands is monotonic.

Carry a new reversal watch that `prior_day_rvol >= 2.0` separates backwards (pass cw 42.9%/14 cl vs fail cw 52.2%/24 cl, widening to −25.4 pp at 2.5); do not act until the passing cell reaches 20 clusters.

Record that Analysis #21 added zero new first-flags in either bucket — all criterion cells reproduce #20 exactly — and consider spacing the next analysis to signal arrival rather than to a fixed cadence, since re-running on an unchanged sample produces no new information.

bounce | POOLED | composite of gap_pct / pct_change_3 / selloff_total_pct | three independently scored criteria | score the COUNT of the three that pass (gap_pct ≤ -0.03, pct_change_3 ≤ -0.15, selloff_total_pct ≤ -0.25) rather than weighting any one of them | 0-of-3 3/13 cw 27.3% (11 cl), 1-of-3 33/47 cw 64.5% (26 cl), 2-of-3 42/46 cw 90.0% (20 cl); the 1→2 step is +25.5 pp with both cells over the 20-cluster gate, while the 2x2 shows gap and pct_change_3 individually add nothing to each other (70.0% / 73.3% / 77.3% across the three non-empty corners). This supersedes the #20 recommendation to promote pct_change_3 alone.

Execute the Large-cap reversal GO suspension — now outstanding at #17 through #22, six cycles. Large runs cw 35.8% over 17 clusters against Medium's cw 68.5% over 18, with no score inversion inside either cap. The cell is still 3 clusters short of the formal gate, which is exactly why six cycles of inaction has cost more than a decision either way would have.

Ship the earliness instrumentation fix — emit `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the per-bucket gate. Unshipped since #18; earliness analysis is now reversal-only for a fifth consecutive cycle because bounce winners still carry no stop-placement data.

Close the #21 watch on moving the bounce entry bar from 4 to 5 — RESOLVED AGAINST raising it. The magnitude gap is real and cluster-robust (score ≥5 cluster-weighted median 3.22R over 21 clusters vs score 4 1.77R over 51; all 52 leave-one-cluster-out refits positive, +1.22R to +1.54R), but score-4 first-flags still run cw 64.6% tradeable at 1.77R. Size by tier, do not exclude. Drop CAUTION first when quantity must be capped.

Emit cluster-weighted `entry_r` by score tier in the pre-aggregated tables — requested at #20 and #21, still row-pooled. I derived it by hand this cycle (table above); it should not need hand-derivation again.

Update the priority_report CLUSTER DAY comment — the 7–14 band it cites as −0.50R/10 sessions has read +0.10R/12 sessions for three straight cycles. Also drop any "monotonic gradient" language: 3–6 (+0.23R) now exceeds 7–14 (+0.10R).
Add the thin-day damp on the 0–2 breadth band (26 sessions, EV −0.24R, win 37.3%) — the only band above 20 sessions. Justify it on its own numbers, not on a cross-band gradient.

Open a bounce watch on `prior_day_range_atr >= 1.0` separating backwards — pass cw 64.2% (30 cl) vs fail cw 73.7% (19 cl). This is a *required* criterion at 1.0 for every cap in both profiles, so a reversed sign matters more than usual. Revisit when the failing cell reaches 20 clusters (currently 19 — one session away).
Keep `selloff_total_pct <= -0.25` (15 clusters, cw 93.3%) and the 0-of-3 / fails-both veto (11 clusters, cw 27.3%) as open watches at 20 clusters. Unchanged from #20.

Stop running this analysis on cadence. Analysis #22 adds zero new first-flags in either bucket — every criterion cell reproduces #20 digit-for-digit, for the second consecutive cycle. The only movement was one new session in the 0–2 breadth band. Trigger the next run on first-flag arrival (suggest: 10 new bounce first-flags or 5 new reversal first-flags), not on a date.

Stop running this analysis on cadence and wire the #22 trigger into the pipeline — fire the next run on 10 new bounce first-flags or 5 new reversal first-flags, not on a date. Analysis #23 adds **zero new first-flags in either bucket for the third consecutive cycle**; the only movement since #22 is the 2026-10-22 session, which contributed two reprints (FJET episode_signal_num=3, PENG =3) and one session to the 0–2 breadth band. Every cap cell, criterion cell and cluster-weighted entry_r tier above reproduces #22 digit-for-digit. Three cycles of analyst time has bought one data point on a band that was already the only one above its sample gate.

Record the bounce entry-bar verdict as answered-with-conditions and close the pooled form of the question — on tradeable_3d the bar is a coin flip (14/25 decided sessions, p≈0.35); on entry_r it is a modest real edge (17/25, +0.85R mean per-session, p≈0.054). Size by score tier per #22; do not use tradeable_3d to defend the bar.

Add the day-conditioning result to the scorer's documentation — the surfaced-vs-control paired edge is +12.3 pp on the 11 sessions where control itself ran ≥55% tradeable and −3.7 pp on the other 15. The bar amplifies breadth rather than selecting within a session, which is the same object the 0–2 breadth damp addresses from the other side.

Record that the control cohort's own score curve (53.6 / 58.9 / 54.7 / 54.4 across scores 0–3, one identical 27-session set) is flat — the cleanest available evidence that the 6-point bounce score does not rank signals below the bar, and that its only defensible role there is as a quantity limiter.

bounce | POOLED | prior_day_range_atr | 1.0 required, all caps, both SETUP_PROFILES | demote to a zero-weight bonus check (do NOT invert to <1.0) | passes ≥1.0 cw 64.2% (30 clusters) vs fails <1.0 cw 75.0% (20 clusters) = −10.8 pp in the wrong direction, both cells now at/over the 20-cluster gate; gate cleared this cycle by `MXL_bounce_2026-10-23` (range 0.477, tradeable) — re-express the bar as 4-of-5 CAUTION / 5-of-5 GO and re-run the cohort tables before shipping

bounce | POOLED | composite of gap_pct / pct_change_3 / selloff_total_pct | three independently scored criteria | score the COUNT of the three that pass (gap_pct ≤ −0.03, pct_change_3 ≤ −0.15, selloff_total_pct ≤ −0.25) rather than weighting any one | 0-of-3 3/13 cw 27.3% (11 cl), 1-of-3 33/47 cw 64.5% (26 cl), 2-of-3 43/47 cw 90.5% (21 cl); 1→2 step +26.0 pp with both cells over the gate; re-affirmed and marginally strengthened versus #22
Ship the `prior_day_range_atr` demotion above — it is the only gated, actionable finding in #24 and the only reason this cycle produced value.

Replace the cadence trigger with a cell-gate watcher. #22/#23 asked to fire the next run on 10 new bounce first-flags or 5 new reversal first-flags; #24 arrived with 1 and 0, so that trigger would have deferred the `prior_day_range_atr` resolution indefinitely. The right mechanism is narrower: watch the *named open cells* (`prior_day_range_atr` fail, `selloff_total_pct ≤ −0.25`, 0-of-3 veto, reversal `prior_day_rvol ≥ 2.0`, reversal Large cap) and fire when any crosses 20 clusters. That costs one query per session instead of a full analyst cycle, and it is what #22 was actually predicting when it wrote "one session away."

Force the Large-cap reversal GO decision — outstanding #17 through #24, seven cycles. Large cw 35.8%/17 clusters vs Medium cw 68.5%/18 clusters. With reversal first-flags arriving at zero per cycle the cell will not reach 20 clusters on its own; continuing to defer is itself a decision to keep trading the worse cap. Either suspend Large-cap reversal GO on the 17-cluster evidence and label it provisional, or record explicitly that it will be traded unchanged until the drought ends.

Ship the earliness instrumentation fix — emit `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the per-bucket gate. Unshipped since #18; bounce earliness has now been unanalyzable for six consecutive cycles because bounce winners carry no stop-placement data.

Emit cluster-weighted `entry_r` by score tier in the pre-aggregated tables. Requested at #20, #21 and #22, still row-pooled at #24. `entry_r` is heavily right-skewed and the score-5 jump to 2.50R is the single number driving the size-by-tier policy — it cannot be audited for cluster concentration without this.

Update the priority_report CLUSTER DAY comment. The 7–14 band it cites as −0.50R/10 sessions now reads +0.10R/12 sessions — opposite sign, fourth consecutive cycle. Mark the band single-session-sensitive and unusable as justification for the 7→15 raise, and delete any "monotonic gradient" language: 3–6 (+0.27R) exceeds both 7–14 (+0.10R) and 15+ (+0.24R).
Add the thin-day damp on the 0–2 breadth band — 27 sessions, EV −0.34R, win 35.2%, the only band above the 20-session gate and stably negative across #21/#22/#24. Justify on that cell alone.

Document the CLUSTER DAY 15-window threshold as judgment-set and unvalidated. The 15+ band stands at 3 sessions and is not on a path to 20; leaving a stale empirical claim attached to it invites a fifth cycle of sign-flip reporting.

Emit a T1-equivalent reversal gate (0.5×ATR) alongside the 1.0×ATR gate for reporting comparability only. The 46.4% reversal and 74.8% bounce headlines currently use gates that differ by ~2× in ATR terms; median non-tradeable reversal first-flag MFE is 0.62 ATR with 35% reaching ≥0.75 ATR, so the buckets are not comparable as published. Reporting change, not a trading change.

Add a standing note to the bounce performance headline that `bounce_2026-07-28` (19/19) and `bounce_2026-07-17` (13/13) supply 36% of all bounce first-flag wins from 2 of 46 clusters, and that the cluster-weighted 68.0% is the quotable figure.

bounce | POOLED | prior_day_range_atr | 1.0 required, all caps, both SETUP_PROFILES | demote to zero-weight bonus check (do NOT invert to <1.0) | pass ≥1.0 cw 64.2% (30 clusters) vs fail <1.0 cw 75.0% (20 clusters) = −10.8 pp wrong-signed, both cells gated; unchanged from #24, carried not re-derived; re-express the bar as 4-of-5 CAUTION / 5-of-5 GO and re-run the cohort tables before shipping
Ship the `prior_day_range_atr` demotion. It was the only gated actionable finding in #24, it is unchanged in #25, and a cycle spent re-reporting it is a cycle wasted.

Stop running this analysis on cadence and implement the #24 cell-gate watcher — one query per session over the named open cells (`prior_day_range_atr` fail, `selloff_total_pct ≤ −0.25`, 0-of-3 veto, reversal `prior_day_rvol ≥ 2.0`, reversal Large cap) plus the 0–2 breadth band, firing when any crosses its gate. #25 is the third zero-first-flag cycle in four and reproduced every criterion cell from #24; the watcher would have skipped it outright.

Force the Large-cap reversal GO decision — now outstanding #17 through #25, eight cycles. Large cw 35.8%/17 clusters vs Medium cw 68.5%/18 clusters, with reversal first-flags arriving at zero per cycle. The cell will not reach 20 clusters. Either suspend Large-cap reversal GO on the 17-cluster evidence and label it provisional, or record explicitly that it will be traded unchanged until the drought ends. Deferring again is itself a decision to keep trading the worse cap.

Ship the bounce earliness instrumentation — emit `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the per-bucket gate. Unshipped since #18; bounce earliness is now unanalyzable for the sixth consecutive cycle because `tradeable_3d=True` bounce rows that never reached 1 ATR carry blanks in both existing columns.

Emit cluster-weighted `entry_r` by score tier. Requested at #20, #21, #22, #24 and now #25. The score-5 median of 2.50R is the sole basis for size-by-tier and cannot be audited for cluster concentration without it.

Ship the 0–2 breadth damp — 28 sessions, EV −0.20R, win 37.9%, the only band above the session gate and negative in all four readings. Size the damp to the sign, not to #24's −0.34R; the magnitude has moved ±0.14R per session added across cycles.

Fix the priority_report CLUSTER DAY comment — the 7–14 band it cites as −0.50R/10 sessions now reads +0.10R/12 sessions (fifth consecutive opposite-sign cycle). Mark it single-session-sensitive, delete it as justification for the 7→15 raise, remove any "monotonic gradient" language (3–6 at +0.27R exceeds both higher bands), and document the 15-window threshold as judgment-set and unvalidated at 3 sessions.

Record the updated day-conditioning result in the scorer documentation — the surfaced-vs-control paired edge is **+10.5 pp on the 13 sessions where control itself ran ≥55% tradeable (11/13 won, p = 0.022)** and **−3.7 pp on the other 15 (4/15 won)**. Strengthened versus #23 (was 11 and 15 sessions at +12.3 / −3.7). The bar amplifies breadth rather than selecting within a session. Both cells under the 20-session gate — watch, not a change.

Update the entry-bar verdict record — on `tradeable_3d` the bar is a coin flip (15/27 decided sessions, p = 0.70, 28 paired sessions, question answered not open); on `entry_r` it is a modest edge that is **not strengthening** (18/27, +0.83R mean, p = 0.122, versus 17/25 / p ≈ 0.11 at #23). Size by score tier; never defend the bar on `tradeable_3d`.

Emit a T1-equivalent reversal gate (0.5×ATR) alongside the 1.0×ATR gate for reporting comparability only — 13/23 (57%) of visible non-tradeable reversal first-flags reached ≥0.5 ATR. Reporting change, not a trading change.

Add the standing cluster-concentration note to the bounce headline — `bounce_2026-07-28` (19/19) and `bounce_2026-07-17` (13/13) supply 26.9% of bounce first-flags and 36.0% of its wins from 2 of 46 clusters; 68.0% cluster-weighted is the quotable figure.

Restore the omitted-row coverage for reversal earliness, or state the limit in the output contract — the signal-outcomes table omits 85 older surfaced rows, leaving only 53 of 97 reversal first-flags visible, and that subset runs 56.6% tradeable against the cohort's 46.4%. Earliness levels computed here are optimistic; only the shape is trustworthy.

Ship the bounce `prior_day_range_atr` demotion. It is now the only gated actionable finding for the third consecutive cycle (#24, #25, #26) and has been re-reported three times without a change landing.

Stop running this analysis on cadence; implement the #24 cell-gate watcher — one query per session over the named open cells (bounce `prior_day_range_atr` fail, bounce `selloff_total_pct ≤ −0.25`, 0-of-3 veto, reversal `prior_day_rvol ≥ 2.0`, reversal Large cap, the control-≥55% day-conditioning cell) plus the 0–2 breadth band, firing when any crosses its gate. #26 is the fourth low-first-flag cycle in five and reproduced every criterion cell from #25.

Force the Large-cap reversal GO decision — now outstanding #17 through #26, nine cycles. Large cw 35.8% / 17 clusters vs Medium cw 68.5% / 18 clusters, with reversal first-flags arriving at ~1 per cycle. The cell will not reach 20 clusters on this trajectory. Either suspend Large-cap reversal GO on the 17-cluster evidence and label it provisional, or record explicitly that it will be traded unchanged until the drought ends. A tenth deferral is itself a decision to keep trading the worse cap.

Ship the bounce earliness instrumentation — emit `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the per-bucket gate. Unshipped since #18; bounce earliness is unanalyzable for the sixth consecutive cycle.

Emit cluster-weighted `entry_r` by score tier in the pre-aggregated tables. Requested at #20, #21, #22, #24, #25, now #26. The score-5 median of 2.50R is the sole basis for size-by-tier, is non-monotonic against score 6 (1.72R), and cannot be audited for cluster concentration without it.

Revise the 0–2 breadth damp recommendation from #25 — EV has decayed −0.34R → −0.20R → −0.06R across three readings while sessions grew 27 → 28 → 29. Implement at most a token damp justified on the stable negative sign, or hold the cell to 35 sessions. Do not size a damp off −0.06R.

Fix the priority_report CLUSTER DAY comment — delete the 7–14 = −0.50R/10-session claim (now +0.10R/12 sessions, sixth opposite-sign cycle) as justification for the 7→15 raise, remove any monotonic-gradient language (3–6 at +0.27R exceeds both higher bands), and document the 15-window threshold as judgment-set and unvalidated at 3 sessions.

Record the updated entry-bar verdict — on `tradeable_3d` the bar is a coin flip (16/28 decided sessions, p ≈ 0.57, 29 paired sessions; question answered, not open). On `entry_r` it is a modest edge that **weakened** this cycle (18/28, p ≈ 0.19, versus 18/27 / p ≈ 0.12 at #25 and 17/25 / p ≈ 0.11 at #23). Size by score tier; never defend the bar on `tradeable_3d`.

Record the strengthened day-conditioning result in the scorer documentation — paired edge **+11.2 pp on the 14 sessions where control itself ran ≥55% tradeable (12/14 won, p = 0.013)** vs **−3.7 pp on the other 15 (4/15 won, 10 lost)**. Third consecutive strengthening reading (#23 +12.3/11, #25 +10.5/13, #26 +11.2/14). The bar amplifies breadth rather than selecting within a session. Both cells under the 20-session gate — watch, and note the low-breadth cell is dominated by sessions with surfaced n ≤ 2 (8 of 15).

Emit a T1-equivalent reversal gate (0.5×ATR) alongside the 1.0×ATR gate for reporting comparability only — 16/26 (61.5%) of visible non-tradeable reversal first-flags reached ≥0.5 ATR, which would move the visible reversal rate from 54.4% to 82.5%. Reporting change, not a trading change. Sixth cycle requested.

Restore omitted-row coverage for reversal earliness, or state the limit in the output contract — 87 older surfaced rows are omitted, leaving 57 of 98 reversal first-flags visible, and that subset runs 54.4% tradeable against the cohort's 46.9%. Earliness levels computed here are optimistic by ~7–8 pp; only the shape is trustworthy.

Add the standing cluster-concentration note to the bounce performance headline — `bounce_2026-07-28` (19/19) and `bounce_2026-07-17` (13/13) supply 26.9% of bounce first-flags and 36.0% of its wins from 2 of 46 clusters; 68.0% cluster-weighted is the quotable figure.
